query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of Cr to a refractory high-entropy alloy can improve its dynamic strength-ductility performance by forming a Laves phase that enhances strength and ductility.
generation.mechanism: Solid solution hardening and formation of a continuous reticulated structure of the Laves phase that hinders crack propagation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength and fracture strain
generation.baseline: HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy without Cr addition
generation.boundary: Limited to refractory high-entropy alloys with similar composition and processing conditions
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of the Laves phase formation and its effect on the alloy's properties is not fully understood

falsification_experiment.design: Compression testing of HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy with and without Cr addition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of Cr does not result in a significant improvement in yield strength and fracture strain, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does the addition of Cr to the HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy affect its phase composition, microstructure, and room-temperature mechanical properties, specifically regarding the synergy between strength and ductility?. System: HfMoTaTiZr (30.0 at% Hf, 16.1 at% Mo, 30.4 at% Ta, 8.1 at% Ti, 15.4 at% Zr) and HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 (28.8 at% Hf, 15.5 at% Mo, 29.1 at% Ta, 7.7 at% Ti, 14.7 at% Zr, 4.2 at% Cr). Processing: Vacuum arc melting in an inert gas atmosphere; ingots re-melted at least 5 times to improve chemical homogeneity; weight loss did not exceed 0.5 wt%. Test conditions: Room temperature; Vickers hardness with 0.3 kg load and 15 s dwelling time; compression tests on cylindrical samples (3 mm diameter, 6 mm height) at a ram speed of 0.008 mm s−1 (strain rate 0.001/s). Findings: The addition of 4.2 at% Cr led to the formation of a Laves phase in addition to the BCC phase, whereas the base alloy was single-phase BCC.; The hardness of HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 reached 535.8 Hv0.3, which is 56.96% higher than the reference alloy HfMoTaTiZr (460.1 Hv0.3).; The yield strength of HfMoTaTiZrCr0.5 reached 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa, which is 207.5 MPa higher than HfMoTaTi
